subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core add built-in pace-aware resource governance for autonomous agents, and should the first shipped surface be visibility-only or enforcement-capable?
rationale: The request changes provider usage semantics, autonomous throttling behavior, persisted state ownership, status/session_status UX, and public config defaults, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/API boundary.

options.title: Visibility First
options.body: Expose pace/projection context through status and agent context first, then defer blocking/throttling until the policy and recovery semantics are proven.

options.title: Full Core Enforcement
options.body: Design an opt-in core admission layer that can block or throttle subagents/non-interactive runs with persisted state, notifications, and upgrade-safe config.

options.title: Plugin Or Skill Boundary
options.body: Keep core limited to provider usage APIs and route pace-specific workflows to a skill or plugin unless a missing core hook is identified.

recommendation.title: Visibility First
recommendation.body: Expose pace/projection context through status and agent context first, then defer blocking/throttling until the policy and recovery semantics are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest observed product/config/status boundary history among the related code paths and prior related reviews.
